source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Document the date and time of the failed safety check.
3. Identify the electrical appliance by brand, model, and serial number.
4. Record the location of the appliance within the premises (e.g., Kitchen, Living Room).
5. Describe the specific tests performed during the safety check (e.g., insulation resistance test, polarity check, earth continuity test).
6. Note the safety standards and regulations that are applicable (e.g., IEC 60335, NFPA 70, BS EN 60065).
7. Record the results of each test, particularly highlighting the failure points (e.g., failed insulation resistance test with a reading of 0.5 MΩ, well below the minimum threshold of 1 MΩ).
8. Capture photos or videos of the failure points or any visible issues (e.g., damaged cords, scorched outlets).
9. Include observations and comments that may have contributed to the failures (e.g., inadequate wiring
